summary: Iteration 4 — Master Admin / Site Admin / multi-site backend endpoints. 42/42 NEW tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_master_admin_sites.py and FULL regression suite is 85/85 across backend_test.py (15), test_new_features.py (13), test_iter3_features.py (15), test_master_admin_sites.py (42). Coverage: login (all 4 roles), sites CRUD, role-scoped /sites listing (master sees all; site_admin sees own; vendor sees mapped only), single-site GET access boundaries, PATCH site (toggles allow_pre_order/cash_carry verified), vendor-site mapping (create/duplicate-400/list/unmap), meal schedule GET defaults + PUT update + GET verification, Site Menu GET (master/site/employee/vendor), Excel upload (.xlsx generated via openpyxl, 6 rows inserted, missing-columns rejected w/ 400), PATCH /menu/{id}/site-control (is_available/price/show_price persisted; cross-site site_admin gets 403), Admin Management (create site_admin/super_admin/master_admin, master email constraint enforced w/ 400, non-master 403, seed admin delete blocked w/ 400, site_admin delete-attempt 403, list + cleanup), Reports (master-dashboard contains all 9 required keys, site report contains all 5 keys, role 403s verified), /employee/my-site (returns site+vendors+meal_schedule+current_meal_period+ordering_modes, non-employees 403), AuthZ boundaries, legacy regression (vendor /menu/vendor/all + /orders).

minor.issue: Does not validate that site_id exists (find_one result is ignored). Submitting a bogus site_id silently creates a dangling site_admin user.
No validation that assigned_sites IDs actually exist.

Allows site_admin/super_admin to also patch (because can_access_site returns true for owners). Intended behavior per spec is master/site_admin only — verify and lock down `status` field to master only (a site_admin could mark its own site inactive).
Returns 200 even when no mapping existed (no 404); idempotent but masks bad requests.
Employee role returns the employee's site object — review_request expected 403 or filtered; current impl returns filtered list (acceptable, but doc the contract).
vendor_id query param is not validated to actually belong to a mapped vendor; any vendor_id string is accepted.
can_access_site() returns False for an employee at that site unless an `or` branch in the route handler covers it; relies on the route-level OR. Fine, but the helper itself is misleading.

action_items: Validate site_id in POST /admin/site-admins (currently fetched but result ignored).
Lock `status` field in PATCH /sites/{id} to master_admin only (site_admin should not be able to deactivate their own site).
Validate that vendor_id in upload-excel query is actually mapped to the site (defense in depth).
Optional: split server.py (now ~2450 lines) into routers for /sites, /admin, /reports, /menu — code maintainability suffering.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2448 lines — long-overdue split into routers (auth, sites, admin, menu, reports, orders).
POST /admin/site-admins line 2160: `await db.sites.find_one(...)` result is discarded, comment claims 'validates' but it doesn't raise if site is None.
current_meal_period() uses now.astimezone() without timezone arg; on server with UTC tz this stays UTC even though business intent is IST — possible bug for meal-period-aware features.
Excel upload accepts any vendor_id string; no check vs db.vendors or vendor-site mapping.
GET /sites/{id} 403 logic mixes can_access_site with an inline employee check (line 1941). Move employee-of-site into can_access_site for consistency.
DELETE /sites/{id}/vendors/{vendor_id} should return 404 if the mapping doesn't exist (current impl always 200).
test_credentials: Used /app/memory/test_credentials.md (master/site/vendor/employee). Note: NOTE — the seed master_admin (admin@cravitoo.com) is referred to as super_admin in /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py history; actual role is master_admin. Test creds file is correct.
seed_data_creation: Created during run (most cleaned up): 1 TEST_Site_xxxxxx site (still present, kept for future runs as no DELETE /sites endpoint exists), 6 TEST_Dish_* menu items at that site (deleted in cleanup phase via DELETE /menu/{id}), 1 test site_admin user (created+deleted), 1 test super_admin user (created+deleted), 1 test master_admin user @cravitoo.com (created+deleted). Vendor-site mapping created, then unmapped during authZ test, then re-mapped, then unmapped again at the end. NOTE: TEST_Site cannot be deleted via API — no DELETE /sites/{id} endpoint exists.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v` for the full 85-test regression. The new master/site admin tests are in test_master_admin_sites.py; they create a fresh TEST_Site_<uuid> each run (since no DELETE /sites endpoint exists, expect TEST_Site_* sites to accumulate in DB over runs — could add cleanup if a DELETE /sites endpoint is added). Login response shape is flat (access_token + user fields at top level) not nested; the helper in test_master_admin_sites.py reshapes it.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — all functional tests pass. Two action items flagged: site_admins endpoint doesn't enforce site_id existence; PATCH /sites allows status changes by site_admin. Both are AuthZ / input-validation gaps, not functional bugs.
